title: MSFT Stock Gets A Thumbs Up From Barclays – Firm Expects Quarter To Start Showing ‘More Differentiation’ In Software - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft (MSFT) is drawing investor attention after Barclays raised its price target on the stock to $600 from $512 while maintaining an 'Overweight' rating. Barclays adjusted the target as part of its third-quarter software earnings preview, and said the quarter “should start showing more differentiation in software,” according to The Fly. MSFT shares were trading 1.5% higher at the time of writing on Tuesday. Microsoft's market capitalization reached $4.02 trillion at Monday's close, surpassing the $4 trillion threshold for the first time since October 2025. Barclays’ latest note follows analyst updates from Deutsche Bank and Phillip Securities on Monday, according to The Fly. Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick raised his price target to $600 from $550 while maintaining a 'Buy' rating. The move was part of the firm’s first-quarter earnings preview. Phillip Securities downgraded Microsoft to 'Neutral' from 'Accumulate' and set a $515 price target, citing the recent re-rating of the shares. Microsoft, Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Oracle (ORCL) announced on Tuesday that they have established a working group under the Open Compute Project (OCP) to develop an open specification for an integrated hardware security module (HSM) for cloud and hyperscale data centers. The proposed solution is designed to support secure cryptographic key caching and key lifecycle management at the server level. The companies said the approach aims to reduce latency, improve scalability and strengthen cloud workload security. The working group plans to define an open specification incorporating a hardware security boundary, key vault and attestation chain directly into servers. The companies are targeting an initial draft for the October 2026 OCP Global Summit, with version 1.0 to follow. On Monday, Microsoft announced plans to scale its Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027. The company said Maia 200 is already serving production workloads, including Microsoft Copilot, while Maia 300 is expected to begin production deployments in 2027. Microsoft said it expects Maia 300 to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Microsoft is expected to report its fiscal first-quarter (Q1) 2027 results after the closing bell on Oct. 28, 2026. According to Fiscal AI, analysts expect earnings of around $4.72 per share on revenue of approximately $90.4 billion. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) shares drew significant investor attention on Tuesday after Piper Sandler downgraded the satellite communications company, raising concerns about its ability to meet its ambitious satellite launch schedule amid growing competition from SpaceX (SPCX). According to The Fly, Piper Sandler downgraded ASTS to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Overweight’ and slashed its price target to $54 from $98, citing reduced confidence in the company’s satellite deployment plans for 2026 and 2027. ASTS shares were down 9% at the time of writing, having shed more than 17% since the SpaceX update was made public. Piper said it is concerned about AST SpaceMobile due to SpaceX’s ambitions in the direct-to-cell market following its agreement to acquire Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio for approximately $8 billion. The acquisition, subject to regulatory approval, could help Starlink Mobile combine satellite connectivity with traditional ground-based wireless networks. Piper warned that SpaceX could theoretically limit launch opportunities for competitors such as AST, potentially slowing its satellite deployment. SpaceX could also pressure service pricing by competing more aggressively with traditional telecom operators. However, the brokerage remains constructive on AST’s longer-term prospects beyond 2027. AST SpaceMobile has partnerships with more than 60 mobile operators covering over three billion subscribers globally. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits surrounding ASTS turned ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ a day earlier, amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes. ASTS was also among the top trending tickers on the platform at the time of writing. One user said Piper Sandler’s downgrade overstates the launch risk. Another user said the stock hasn’t bottomed out yet. However, some analysts have remained bullish on ASTS stock. On Monday, Deutsche Bank upgraded ASTS to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ and maintained a $93 price target. Analyst Bryan Kraft viewed the recent selloff as a buying opportunity, citing positive developments that investors may have overlooked. Berenberg also reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating, arguing that SpaceX’s expansion could make the firm a more attractive satellite partner for existing wireless carriers. AST SpaceMobile recently launched satellites through BlueBird 13, while BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 are positioned for upcoming launches from Florida. The company previously targeted around 45 satellites in orbit by year-end 2026. AST SpaceMobile has a contracted revenue backlog of about $1.3 billion and expects revenue of $150 million to $200 million in full-year 2026. Verizon (VZ), Comcast (CMCSA), T-Mobile US (TMUS) and Charter Communications (CHTR) received price target cuts from Bernstein on Tuesday, citing growing competition from SpaceX’s (SPCX) planned entry into the U.S. mobile carrier market. Bernstein reiterated its ‘Market Perform’ rating on all four stocks, according to a note cited by The Fly. The firm said competitive pressure from SpaceX was compounded by recent pricing moves from incumbent carriers and expected fourth-quarter seasonality. Despite the bearish commentary, CHTR stock led gains among the cohort, up 2.3% in morning trade. TMUS stock was up 1.4%, CMCSA stock gained 1%, and VZ stock edged 0.5% higher. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TMUS and VZ shares trended in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day. Sentiment around CHTR slipped to ‘bearish’ from the ‘neutral’ zone, while sentiment around CMCSA remained in ‘neutral’ territory. The price target cuts follow SpaceX’s announcement last week that it plans to expand Starlink into a major U.S. mobile carrier. The company said it was acquiring a low-band spectrum portfolio in the 800 MHz band, which it said would close the remaining technical gap. The announcement triggered a sharp selloff in major wireless stocks on Friday. The three largest U.S. carriers fell by double digits, shedding more than $50 billion in combined market value. Verizon recorded its steepest one-day decline since 2002. Analysts have differed on how quickly SpaceX could become a meaningful threat to established carriers. Raymond James called concerns about a near-term challenge to T-Mobile “overblown,” while Morningstar said Verizon’s existing network gives established operators a significant advantage. “We believe the recent fears over competition from SpaceX are overblown, as they are 3+ years away from becoming reality, and competition from larger players is nothing new to T-Mobile,” Raymond James said. The firm upgraded T-Mobile to 'Outperform' from 'Market Perform' and set a $170 price target. Morningstar said the spectrum deal adds uncertainty for wireless carriers but maintained its base case that Starlink would not threaten their wireless operations. It raised its uncertainty ratings for Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T to 'High' from 'Medium', noting that SpaceX still needs more spectrum and thousands of sites to build a competitive terrestrial network. JPMorgan said that without a deal with an existing carrier, SpaceX would likely need to build a ground network using macro towers. SpaceX is targeting 2027 for its next-generation satellites, with upgraded service expected by the end of that year. Apple (AAPL) shares climbed about 2% to a new record high on Tuesday after the company unveiled several new smart home products at its October 13 "Welcome Home" event, expanding its presence in connected-home devices. The announcements included the new HomeView smart display, an updated HomePod mini 2 speaker, a refreshed Apple TV 4K and a range of home accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. At the time of this writing, AAPL stock was trading 1% higher at around $344. The $299 HomeView marks Apple's entry into dedicated smart home displays, combining entertainment, video calling and household device controls in a single product. Powered by Apple's updated Siri artificial intelligence (AI) assistant, the device can also manage connected accessories such as cameras, doorbells and thermostats. It will become available on November 13. Apple also refreshed two existing products after several years without major updates. The $149 HomePod mini 2 is the first update to the speaker since its 2020 introduction, while the new Apple TV 4K marks the first refresh of Apple's TV set-top box since 2022. The HomePod mini 2 will become available on October 30, although its new Siri AI capabilities will arrive through a future software update. The updated Apple TV 4K will be available on November 13. Apple also announced its Home Collection, developed with LG and Schneider Electric, featuring security cameras, smart locks, video doorbells and thermostats. The accessories will begin rolling out in December. The launch comes as Apple competes with Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOG, GOOGL) in the smart home market. Reuters reported that Apple's earlier efforts faced challenges related to Siri's functionality and compatibility with third-party devices. Apple does not separately disclose revenue from its home products; instead, it includes them in its broader Wearables, Home and Accessories category. The category generated $7.88 billion in Apple's fiscal third quarter ended June 27, up 6% from $7.40 billion a year earlier. That represented about 7.2% of Apple's total quarterly revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year over year. The latest launches also come shortly after a leadership transition at Apple. John Ternus took over as CEO on September 1, succeeding Tim Cook, who moved into the executive chairman role. Ternus previously led Apple's hardware engineering division, overseeing development across several major product lines. The new home lineup is among Apple's first major product introductions under Ternus. Apple has not disclosed revenue targets for HomeView or the broader smart home expansion. title: MSFT Stock Rebounds Above $520 as Microsoft's Anthropic Commitment Reaches $44.9 Billion - FXLeaders
content: Microsoft shares have recovered sharply after falling toward $500, reclaiming losses with a 3% rebound as investors assess a reported $44.9 billion Anthropic computing commitment against rising infrastructure costs, custom-chip investment and growing concerns about the returns from data-centre expansion. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) shares have experienced significant volatility after initially climbing above $550 in mid-October following stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings. However, the rally quickly reversed, with the stock falling toward $500 on Monday as investors reassessed infrastructure spending and the financial returns from expanding computing capacity. The decline followed renewed pressure across technology stocks after Apple’s and Palantir’s earnings, although Microsoft has recovered sharply on Tuesday, gaining approximately 3% and reclaiming the $520 level. The rebound comes as investors digest new disclosures concerning Microsoft’s relationship with Anthropic. An amended filing identifies at least $44.9 billion in commitments to Microsoft through June 2033, subject to contractual delivery and breach provisions. The disclosure highlights the scale of future computing demand, although it relates to an existing arrangement amended during 2026. The recovery also comes ahead of the US midterm elections, which could influence broader market sentiment and expectations surrounding technology regulation, government spending and economic policy. Microsoft reported net income of $36.6 billion, or $4.92 per diluted share, representing a 32% increase year over year on a GAAP basis. Non-GAAP earnings reached $4.89 per share, excluding the impact of investments in OpenAI. Revenue increased to $90.6 billion from $77.6 billion a year earlier, meeting analyst expectations, while earnings comfortably exceeded the consensus forecast of $4.27 per share. Despite the strong results, the market reaction demonstrated that investors are becoming more demanding. Earnings growth alone may no longer be sufficient to justify Microsoft’s premium valuation if infrastructure expenses continue increasing faster than expected returns. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion, increasing 30% year over year, or 31% in constant currency. Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said the company exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income and earnings per share. CEO Satya Nadella also highlighted improvements in computing capacity, customer choice, security and cost efficiency. Nevertheless, investors want evidence that strong cloud demand can translate into sustainable profitability. Expanding data-centre capacity requires substantial capital, and the financial benefits depend on how quickly Microsoft can monetise that investment. The reported $44.9 billion commitment from Anthropic provides an important indication of the potential demand for Microsoft’s computing infrastructure. However, the broader industry faces questions about financing and the sustainability of spending. Elon Musk recently warned that smaller cloud infrastructure providers could struggle to survive as competition increases and financing becomes more difficult. His comments reflect concerns that companies relying heavily on debt to finance data-centre construction could face pressure if customer demand or revenue growth fails to meet expectations. For Microsoft, the challenge is balancing substantial future commitments with the need to maintain attractive margins and generate sufficient cash flow. Microsoft is also developing its Maia 300 processor to improve computing efficiency and reduce dependence on external chip suppliers. The processor reportedly targets 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, while its 96-accelerator configuration is designed to deliver significantly higher rack-scale throughput than Maia 200. Custom silicon could eventually reduce Microsoft’s infrastructure costs, although development and deployment require substantial investment before the benefits become visible. Microsoft has also reportedly discussed leasing computing capacity from SpaceX, although the status of those discussions remains unclear. Microsoft shares jumped above the critical $500 level as they rebounded strongly in the last 2 months which has now turned into a support zone, and climbed above $550 earlier in October but slipped toward $500 again yesterday. The price slip breached the 50 daily SMA in yellow in September which has been acting as support and we’re seeing a rebound today. The $550 area represents both psychological and technical resistance so for now MAFT buyers gave up at this zone, revering lower. Not all divisions are delivering the same growth. Microsoft’s Devices and Consumer segment generated $15.5 billion in revenue, declining 3% year over year. Search and advertising revenue increased 12%, but Xbox content and services revenue declined 2%, while Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 22%. Regulatory pressure is another concern. The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has proposed designating Microsoft as having strategic market status in certain software markets, potentially increasing scrutiny of licensing, pricing and product bundling. Competition from Google Workspace could also challenge Microsoft’s business software operations as companies reassess subscription costs and available alternatives. Microsoft’s latest rebound above $520 suggests buyers are returning after the stock approached $500. Strong cloud growth and the Anthropic commitment provide evidence of continued demand for computing infrastructure. However, the larger challenge remains profitability. Investors are increasingly questioning whether enormous data-centre investments can generate sufficient returns to justify current valuations. A sustained recovery will depend on Microsoft’s ability to convert cloud demand into stronger cash generation while controlling infrastructure costs. Without clearer evidence of improving investment returns, the stock could remain vulnerable to further volatility despite its strong underlying earnings.

title: PLTR Stock Gets Fresh Price Target Hikes, But Jefferies Favors MSFT, ORCL, SNOW Shares - Stocktwits
content: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) shares fell in morning trading on Tuesday, putting the stock on track to hit its lowest level since September, even as analysts raised their price targets following the company’s third-quarter results. Citi, Morgan Stanley, Piper Sandler and RBC Capital all lifted their targets, but Jefferies kept its target steady at $80 with an ‘Underperform’ rating, according to TheFly. The firm said that while Palantir delivered a "strong" quarter, the debate has shifted from whether customers want Palantir’s software to whether the company can sustain accelerating growth against tougher comparisons. Jefferies said it sees “more compelling” risk and reward elsewhere in Microsoft (MSFT), Oracle (ORCL), and Snowflake (SNOW). According to the firm, they offer strong long-term growth at more attractive valuations. PLTR stock dropped around 5% in morning trade and was among the top-trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. Palantir reported revenue growth accelerating for the 13th consecutive quarter. Revenue grew 96% year over year in the third quarter (Q3) to $2.31 billion, beating market expectations of $2.17 billion, according to Koyfin. The company also raised its full-year revenue forecast to $8.53 billion from about $8.15 billion, its third increase this year. It expects fourth-quarter (Q4) revenue of about $2.65 billion. Citi, which raised its target to $265 from $250 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating, called the results “another top-line blowout,” driven by U.S. commercial and government sales. Morgan Stanley analyst Sanjit Singh called revenue growth for a 13th consecutive quarter “impressive.” The main concern for Wall Street was bookings, which indicate future business. Total contract value (TCV), which measures the value of deals signed during the quarter, rose 6% year over year to $2.92 billion, down sharply from 49% growth in the second quarter. U.S. commercial TCV increased 11%. According to Morgan Stanley, PLTR stock’s reaction reflected elevated expectations for U.S. commercial sales and slower bookings growth linked to shorter contracts. Meanwhile, RBC Capital highlighted remaining deal value grew just 2% from the second quarter, while remaining performance obligations (RPO) were flat sequentially. The firm also noted management’s acknowledgment that contracts tied to Sovereign AI, Palantir’s work with national governments, were shorter than usual. Piper Sandler said investors will look for evidence in coming quarters that the 11% growth in U.S. commercial bookings “is a fluke of duration and not something structural.” The firm believes the slowdown is related to contract length and said demand for Palantir’s software still “very much outstrip[s] supply.” Citi also described the quarter as strong “despite a duration headwind to bookings.” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PLTR stock flipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’ over the past day, while chatter increased to ‘extremely high’ from ‘normal’ levels. Platform data showed an over 1,100% increase in message volume over the past 24 hours. Some retail traders pushed back against concerns over Palantir's valuation and growth outlook, with some pointing to what they saw as a shift in the criticism of Palantir's business mix. If the PLTR stock's decline holds through the regular session, the shares would give up their year-to-date gains. Veteran market strategist Ed Yardeni warned Monday that a Democratic sweep in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections could deliver a “cold shower for stocks,” arguing that investors have yet to fully price in that possibility. Yardeni said political gridlock could become damaging paralysis, complicating government spending and debt-ceiling negotiations. Prolonged fiscal standoffs could push Treasury yields higher and weigh on equity valuations, he added. He also argued that a Democratic-controlled Congress might do little to constrain President Donald Trump's use of executive authority, citing tariffs and military action against Iran. However, Yardeni said he would view a significant market selloff as a buying opportunity, given the strength of the U.S. economy and corporate earnings. UBS Global Wealth Management assigned a 50% probability to a Democratic sweep, a 40% chance of Democrats winning the House while Republicans retain the Senate, and a 10% probability of Republicans retaining both chambers. In its Monday report, UBS said changes in congressional control could complicate fiscal negotiations, with debt-ceiling discussions in 2027 potentially creating volatility. However, the bank said that narrow congressional majorities and presidential veto power should limit sweeping legislation, while Trump would retain considerable authority over tariffs, foreign policy, and regulation. UBS also expects Treasury yields to settle slightly lower over the next 12 months as easing inflation should outweigh persistent fiscal concerns. The bank said it “would not treat the midterms as a binary directional event” for markets, emphasizing that earnings, economic growth, AI investment and interest rates remain more important drivers. The election also comes amid a pullback in AI stocks. However, UBS does not expect a change in congressional control to derail data-center expansion, as many relevant decisions are made at state and local levels. According to a Reuters report, Citigroup U.S. equity strategist Scott Chronert said stocks would likely react positively if Republicans retained control of the Senate, but negatively if Democrats secured a larger-than-expected Senate majority. “Investors are going into the midterms very cautious,” Indosuez Wealth Management Chief Investment Officer Alexandre Drabowicz told Bloomberg, adding that market fundamentals remain strong and the S&P 500 has historically resumed climbing after elections. title: Bill Ackman on MSFT, AMZN and META: Why Big Tech's Trillion-Dollar AI Spend Is 'Offensive Rather Than Defensive' - TradingView
content: Bill Ackman‘s Pershing Square Inc. PS has said that the artificial intelligence (AI) capital expenditures by Microsoft Corp. MSFT, Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, and Meta Platforms Inc. META are designed to accelerate growth. In a recent shareholder letter, the executives described the projected trillion-dollar outlay by major technology companies as “offensive rather than defensive.” Addressing investor concerns regarding the returns on elevated spending by the hyperscalers, Chief Executive Officer William Ackman and Chief Investment Officer Ryan Israel wrote, “We believe that the hyperscalers’ capital spending is offensive rather than defensive.” The executives stated that “Rather than merely protecting existing franchises, we believe the hyperscalers are investing to accelerate growth and are deploying capital behind a transformative technology that plays directly to their competitive advantages.” The letter detailed how these investments are impacting specific portfolio companies. Regarding AMZN, the executives wrote that “Amazon is extremely well positioned across the AI stack.” They noted that “AI has helped AWS accelerate its revenue growth to 39% in the third quarter.” For META, the letter stated that “Meta’s core digital advertising business has effectively used AI for better ad targeting, generative ad copy, and more effective content recommendation.” Ackman and Israel also noted, “By frontloading its compute investment, Meta has given itself the optionality to scale Muse to a billion or more users.” Regarding MSFT, the executives stated, “Microsoft occupies an enviable position among the hyperscalers in having two large channels by which to monetize its compute.” They noted that “the narrative on the stock has shifted from the company being an AI laggard to an AI leader.” Beyond the hyperscalers, Ackman and Israel highlighted what they view as mispriced opportunities in other portfolio companies. Regarding Uber Technologies Inc. UBER, the executives noted the stock now trades at “its lowest valuation ever.” They stated that investor concerns regarding autonomous vehicles are “increasingly disconnected from its strong business performance.” Ackman and Israel wrote that “the risk due to AVs is minimal,” and projected that Uber’s earnings per share will “compound at 25% or more for the foreseeable future.” Addressing Netflix Inc. NFLX, the letter noted that recent stock declines were driven by investor concerns over plateauing engagement. However, the executives argued that measuring engagement solely by watch time “overshadows the quality of that engagement, which is what ultimately drives the value proposition for Netflix subscribers.” Ackman and Israel concluded that the market “vastly undervalues the company’s growth profile and business quality.” The letter acknowledged concerns over how these companies will fund their infrastructure buildout. Ackman and Israel noted that the hyperscalers are “collectively expected to spend a little over $1 trillion on capital expenditures in 2027 based on consensus estimates.” However, the executives concluded that “The hyperscalers are in a vastly stronger financial position,” adding that they “can finance the substantial majority of their capital expenditures from the prodigious cash flows of their core businesses.” This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors. Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) hit a fresh 52-week low in June, but the company has outperformed the broader equity market ever since. And by the looks of it, Microsoft's run may continue at least a little while longer. The company recently reported its first-quarter 2027 update, and it was impressive. Microsoft gave investors plenty more reasons to buy the stock. Here's what you need to know. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Before looking at the numbers, let's review why Microsoft did not perform well through the first half of the year. Some investors think that artificial intelligence (AI) will disrupt the software industry and replace many services offered by software companies, such as Microsoft. Some recent developments support that view. For instance, a single developer used AI to clone several legacy products in the Microsoft Productivity suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as products from other major software companies, such as Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE). These knock-offs weren't fully functional. Still, it's quite a remarkable achievement, and it highlights why some people are worried about Microsoft's future. The cost of developing software has fallen rapidly thanks to AI, which puts the company at risk. However, so far, Microsoft's financial results suggest that it is doing just fine. In the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Sept. 30, Microsoft's revenue of $92.3 billion increased by 19% year over year. Microsoft's operating income grew 21% year over year to $45.9 billion, while its non-GAAP net earnings per share were $4.89, up 18% year over year. Microsoft debuted a new reporting structure with two segments this quarter. The first, Agents and Infra, did most of the heavy lifting. Revenue from this unit was $76.8 billion, up 25% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenue jumped 30% year over year to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenue grew 48% year over year to $33.2 billion. Microsoft's results beat analyst estimates. But is there more growth ahead for the company? One important metric for Microsoft is remaining performance obligations (RPO), or the amount of contracted revenue that hasn't yet been recognized. This metric indicates demand -- or lack thereof -- for the company's services. By the end of the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, Microsoft had $677 billion in RPO within its Agents and Infra business. Note that this figure grew by 73% year over year. This suggests that AI is not displacing Microsoft's products. Even if the cost of making the kinds of products it has offered for decades has fallen dramatically, there are several advantages for Microsoft. First, it is offering new products that still cost quite a bit. Microsoft offers various AI services through its cloud business, and supporting these products requires substantial investments in AI infrastructure. Second, reproducing a basic knockoff of some of Microsoft's products isn't the same as replacing these products. Millions of businesses have been using Word, Excel, and other Microsoft software services for decades. These are deeply integrated into the day-to-day workflow of these companies. It's not so easy to switch to a clone. In other words, Microsoft benefits from a wide moat thanks to high switching costs and deep, long-standing relationships with enterprises. Third, Microsoft is integrating various AI features into its services, making them more powerful and even harder to replace. There is another important advantage here. Microsoft has direct lines of communication with businesses and access to massive amounts of data, which can help the company determine the best way to improve its services with AI. A single skilled developer cannot easily replicate these advantages, and neither can most major corporations other than Microsoft. So, despite the threat from AI, Microsoft's business remains strong, and the company is riding a tailwind in AI and cloud computing that may persist for a long time. Microsoft's shares are still worth investing in. title: What Could Surprise Microsoft Stock Investors On The Upside? - Trefis

Microsoft (MSFT) stock lost 2.8%, counting dividends, in the year to October 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 11.3%. The business did not stall, with fiscal Q1 2027 revenue rising 18.8% from a year earlier. Microsoft’s next upside may come from contracts customers have already signed, and from demand its data centers cannot yet meet. So how much work is Microsoft still waiting to deliver? Microsoft Has $677 Billion Of Signed Work Still Ahead Microsoft’s commercial backlog, the contracted revenue it has not yet recognized, grew 73% from a year earlier to $677 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, management said on the October 28 call. One large Azure commitment signed in the quarter accounted for part of that total. Commercial bookings fell 12% from a year earlier, a decline management tied to large Azure commitments made in the prior year. Customer demand continues to exceed available supply, management said, which suggests Microsoft could sell more cloud capacity than it has built so far. Microsoft’s cloud computing service, Azure, provides the first proof that this demand turns into sales. Azure revenue grew 48% in the quarter despite delayed capacity, and management said the growth came from Foundry and from better use of its CPUs. Foundry, the platform on which customers build AI solutions with a choice of models, now has over 120,000 customers, and its revenue more than tripled from a year earlier. Microsoft’s Intelligent Cloud segment made up 41.5% of company revenue in fiscal 2026, the year to June 30, 2026, against 37.7% a year earlier. Management also reports Microsoft Cloud revenue, which reached $63.9 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, up 30%. The backlog is also large relative to the whole company. Management said roughly 30% of it will be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months. That works out to about $203 billion, against $346 billion of revenue in Microsoft’s last twelve months. The stock price appears to assume part of this already. Microsoft stock returned 26.4% from May 1 to October 30, 2026, against 5.4% for the S&P 500. On October 30, the stock closed 4.0% below its highest close of the past year. Microsoft is already waiting on capacity. Some third-party capacity it expected in fiscal Q1 2027 was delayed, and management now expects those deliveries in the second half of the fiscal year. Building that capacity is also expensive. Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital projects in fiscal Q1 2027, with $39.4 billion of that paid in cash. Management expects spending of about $170 billion for calendar 2026. A day after the call, Microsoft priced $25 billion of new debt as it pursues that AI buildout. Free cash flow fell to $18.6 billion in the quarter, down from $25.7 billion a year earlier, a drop management tied to the higher capital spending. Cash from operations still rose 29% to $58 billion, management said. Paying for AI by use may also spread more slowly beyond software developers. Asked on the October 28 call whether Microsoft 365 customers will move quickly to usage-based billing, management said that shift will be slower outside of coding, though it still sees encouraging signs. For the upside to show up, Microsoft must add capacity fast enough to turn more of its backlog into sales. When the company reports in January 2027, the number to watch will be Azure growth in constant currency, against management’s guide of 49% to 50% for fiscal Q2 2027. title: INTC, MSFT, META, DASH, VZ: Why Retail Traders Couldn’t Take Their Eyes Off These Stocks Last Week - Stocktwits
content: Technology stocks saw a busy week as Intel Corp. (INTC) shares plunged on a weak outlook, while Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) strong AI and cloud demand raised investor optimism. Meanwhile, Meta Platforms (META), Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), DoorDash Inc. (DASH) and Verizon Communications (VZ) announced major developments. Intel stock crashed 24% after the chipmaker issued a disappointing fourth-quarter (Q4) outlook. Although Q3 revenue climbed 21% year-on-year to $16.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share exceeded expectations, the company warned that supply shortages and declining PC demand would weigh on upcoming results. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company needs to increase production to meet strong demand for its Xeon processors. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, while its Foundry division recorded a 58% increase to $6.7 billion. However, memory shortages and an unexpected shutdown at an Israeli facility disrupted operations. Intel expects PC demand to remain under pressure through at least the first half of 2027. For Q4, it sees revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and adjusted earnings of $0.25 per share. RBC Capital and Goldman Sachs also reduced their price targets on Intel following the weak outlook. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Microsoft delivered a stronger fiscal Q1 2027 performance, with revenue up 19% to $92.3 billion and adjusted earnings of $4.89 per share. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said strong demand for the company’s AI and cloud services drove growth. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenue grew 48%, beating analyst estimates. However, Microsoft increased quarterly spending by 30% to $45.2 billion to build its AI infrastructure. Revenue from its consumer and devices business fell 3%. Billionaire investor Mark Cuban said public companies that audited their health plans found they were being overcharged by insurers such as UnitedHealth Group (UNH), CVS Health (CVS) and Cigna (CI), but refused to tell shareholders about the findings. On a16z’s podcast on Thursday, Cost Plus Drugs co-founder Cuban said he had asked companies to run their insurance and pharmacy benefit contracts through artificial intelligence before signing them, asking where they were being overcharged and what to do about it. Cuban said a couple of the public companies that took his advice were stunned by the results. “There’s a couple public companies that I told to do this and came back to me and were like, ‘Oh my God, we had no idea how badly we were ripped off.’ I'm begging them to mention it on their quarterly earnings conference calls, and they won't do it because they still have to do business with those [insurers]," he said. Cuban did not name any companies. He supports the Break Up Big Medicine Act, which would require insurers to divest pharmacy benefit managers and provider assets. The problem starts with contracts so long that no one can catch every clause, Cuban said. He cited the city of Dallas, which has a PBM contract that tops 1,300 pages. "There's no group of humans with enough coffee on the planet to be able to catch everything they try to squeeze by," he said. CrowdStrike shares closed more than 4% lower in Friday’s regular trading session, Palo Alto Networks shares fell nearly 4%, while Okta shares fell over 6%. According to IO Fund, the first major driver behind the rally is the growing use of AI in cyberattacks and the expanding attack surface companies now have to defend. CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report, cited by IO Fund, found that AI-enabled adversaries increased their operations by 89% in 2025. IBM’s research shows that one in four security breaches is now AI-enabled, with those incidents costing roughly $6 million on average, versus a $4.99 million global average. The threat is also pushing companies to increase spending. IO Fund cited IBM data showing that 85% of organizations plan to raise security spending after learning about the cyber capabilities of frontier AI models, up from 64% in 2025. The shift is becoming particularly important as companies deploy increasingly autonomous AI agents that can write code, access systems and perform tasks with limited human intervention. The firm also pointed to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s warning about the difficulty of securing increasingly capable AI systems: “I no longer think we’re gonna be able to just patch all the bugs,” Altman said during a speech at Stanford Graduate School of Business last month. IO Fund said Gartner expects spending on platforms designed to secure AI systems to climb from about $3 billion in 2026 to $7.7 billion in 2028, suggesting the emerging threat could translate into a substantial new security spending cycle. The other major trend identified by IO Fund is happening inside corporate security departments, which is, customers are increasingly consolidating their spending across broader cybersecurity platforms rather than buying a growing number of point solutions. CrowdStrike’s results offer one indication of the trend, the firm said, adding that CrowdStrike’s annual recurring revenue from its Falcon Flex offering topped $2.2 billion, up 101% year over year, while 51% of its subscription customers now use six or more modules. Net revenue retention among platformized customers exceeded 120%, while Prisma AIRS, its AI security platform, surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue. Blockstream CEO Adam Back said the next big wave of Bitcoin (BTC) buying will come from professional money managers such as pension funds and insurers, adding that this phase is "still largely to come." During an interview with Bitcoin Magazine on Saturday, Back, the inventor of Hashcash, said Bitcoin's first wave of adoption came from "individuals mining or buying Bitcoin OTC or on Bitcoin exchanges." He added that "then, the ETFs brought in a second wave." Spot exchange-traded funds opened Bitcoin up to investors who were used to buying assets through a broker or financial adviser. The third wave, he said, will come through large pools of capital run by professionals. Back noted that several large investment banks have "proposed model portfolios where they would suggest 2 to 4% allocation to Bitcoin." Those allocations could flow into mutual funds that individuals pay into for long-term savings, or "be used by pension funds," he said. Back said that is how many people will end up owning Bitcoin without buying it themselves. "For most people, they are not managing their own investments," he said. Instead, their money is invested "by professional money managers in pension funds, insurance companies, life insurance policies." He added that Bitcoin treasury companies are also part of that picture, since some of those funds buy shares of publicly listed firms that hold Bitcoin. Back said regulation still limits how easily traditional institutions can hold Bitcoin. He pointed to bank capital rules, under which holding Bitcoin for clients "uses up a lot of tier one capital. So, it's quite expensive for them." He said that comes down to global Basel banking rules, which are still adapting to the asset. Back also noted that major custodians of stocks and bonds are starting to move into Bitcoin custody, helped by rule changes in the U.S. over the past year. Bitcoin's price was up 0.7% over 24 hours. Microsoft (NasdaqGS:MSFT) completed a record US$25b multi-tranche bond sale, its first major issuance in nearly a decade. Microsoft runs a global software and cloud platform that underpins everything from workplace productivity to large scale enterprise computing. Fresh capital and new AI partnerships reflect how the company aims to shape the next wave of business and consumer technology usage. Using a large multi tranche bond sale lets Microsoft lock in long term funding for AI data centers and cloud hardware without drawing down as much on current cash. Debt financing also spreads the cost of its US$170b to US$190b calendar 2026 capex plans over time, which can preserve flexibility for dividends, buybacks, or acquisitions. The new fixed and floating rate notes add senior, unsecured liabilities across maturities from 2 to 40 years, which increases total debt but staggers repayment obligations. With a AAA rating and strong earnings, interest costs are supported, although investors still need to watch leverage metrics such as net debt to free cash flow as AI spending continues. One checkpoint is how free cash flow and Microsoft Cloud margins trend over the next four quarters as the US$25b funding is deployed. If Azure and AI related revenue supports operating margin near current levels while net debt to free cash flow remains contained, this would indicate that AI capex is being absorbed without putting undue pressure on the balance sheet.
